# Build and check

## Tools

| Tool | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| Python 3 | The spec and the enclosure |
| Icarus Verilog | Gateware simulation |
| OSS CAD Suite: yosys, nextpnr-ecp5, ecppack, verilator | The bitstream and the whole-chain simulation |
| A C++ compiler | The whole-chain simulation |
| ngspice | The DUT supply simulation |
| Rust | Firmware. The RP2350 binary needs the `thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf` target |
| uv | The enclosure's Python environment |
| gh | Fetches the logo for the enclosure. If `gh` has no access, the build makes the case with a blank top |

## Check the spec

**Bus and pin maps**

```sh
python3 spec/ramspec.py --check
```

**Output**

```text
spec ok: 116 IO lines, 90 legacy roles, 8 socket maps, DIMM needs 109 lines
```

## Simulate the gateware

**14 scenarios**

```sh
gateware/sim/run.sh
```

Each scenario prints one line. The run takes several minutes.

**Last lines of the output**

```text
ok    speed_83: PASS: speed within one tick
ok    detect_fpm: PASS: mode detected
ok    detect_edo: PASS: mode detected
ok    retention: PASS: retention loss detected (64 errors)
```

A scenario that fails prints a line that starts with `FAIL`, and the script exits with status 1.

## Build the bitstream

**Bitstream**

```sh
gateware/build.sh
```

The script tries placement seeds until one meets timing and prints `seed N meets timing`. It fails if no seed reaches 162.5 MHz. The last build reached 163.2 MHz.

## Prove the gateware

**Formal proofs with SymbiYosys**

```sh
gateware/formal/run.sh
```

**Last lines of the output**

```text
PASS  mutant start_dropped: caught by tester_core_props.vh:46
PASS  mutant abort_dropped: caught by tester_core_props.vh:70
PASS  mutant oe_in_write: caught by tester_core_props.vh:83
PASS  mutant drive_no_power: caught by tester_core_props.vh:77
```

The script proves 43 properties of the timing engine and 4 of the SPI register bus for every input, by induction. The run takes about four minutes.

| Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| A start is never lost | A start request in any state runs the step, including during a background refresh |
| An abort is never lost | An abort request ends the access in progress |
| Busy and done | Done never reads true for a step that has not run |
| No dead state | Every state leads back to idle |
| Write and output enable | They never overlap |
| Power-good | Every bus line is released while `DUT_PG` is low |

The four mutant lines inject a fault into the engine and check that a proof catches it. The proofs assume the cycle length is not rewritten in the middle of a cycle. They do not cover the order of the RAS and CAS edges, which depends on register values.

## Simulate the synthesised gateware

**Gate-level scenarios**

```sh
gateware/sim/run_gate.sh        # four scenarios, about 12 minutes
gateware/sim/run_gate.sh all    # all 14, about 47 minutes
```

The script synthesises the top level for the ECP5 and runs the scenarios on that netlist. All 14 pass, with no difference from the source-level run. Yosys has no simulation models for the PLL, the DDR cells or the input delay, so `sim/ecp5_prims_sim.v` stands in for them. Pad latency and PLL behaviour stay unverified until a board runs.

## Test the firmware logic

**32 tests**

```sh
cd firmware
./update-design.sh
cargo test --features sim
```

`update-design.sh` downloads the design system release and generates the display's palette and fonts into `rt-hal/src/generated/`. It needs `gh` and `uv`. Run it once, and again to take a new release.

**Output**

```text
test result: ok. 18 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

The three groups are the test algorithms, the JSON console and the front-panel screens. They run `rt-core` against a software model of the engine and a DRAM. The next section runs the same logic against the real gateware. `rt-fw`, the RP2350 binary, compiles but has not run.

## Simulate the whole chain

**17 scenarios**

```sh
cd firmware/rt-cosim
cargo test
```

**Output**

```text
test result: ok. 17 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

`rt-cosim` runs the firmware's own tests through the real board driver (`rt-hal`) against the real gateware. Verilator compiles `spi_regs.v` and `tester_core.v`, and the crate clocks them at the real tick of 3.077 ns. The run takes about two minutes.

| Part | In the simulation |
| --- | --- |
| Test logic and board driver | The real code: `rt-core` and `rt-hal` |
| SPI register bus | Bit by bit at 4 MHz into the real `spi_regs.v` |
| Timing engine | The real `tester_core.v` |
| DDR pad cells | A software model: two output phases, two input samples, the fine input delay |
| Cartridge | A software model: drive and receive buffers with fixed delays, byte-lane enables, weak pulls, sense read-back |
| DRAM | A pin-level model: access time, FPM or EDO outputs, retention, injected faults |
| DUT supply | Ideal parts: DAC, regulator set point, switch, over-voltage veto, current monitor |

The scenarios cover a 4-bit chip, a 1-bit chip with separate data in and out, a 30-pin SIMM with parity and a 36-bit EDO 72-pin SIMM. The fault scenarios are a stuck cell, shorted data lines, a dead address line, and shorted and stuck control lines. The rest are an empty socket, a part that is too slow, an overcurrent, the supply margin test and the retention test.

The simulation does not model signal quality, the PLL, the ECP5 pad primitives or supply ramps. `rt-fw` is not part of it.

## Simulate the DUT supply

**ngspice checks**

```sh
hardware/spice/run.sh
```

The script prints one `PASS`, `FAIL` or `INFO` line per check and exits with status 1 if a check fails. The regulator is a behavioural model and the transistors are generic models. The lines marked `ASSUMED` in `hardware/spice/rail.inc` list every value that does not come from the board.

All checks pass. [Limits of revision A](../guides/bring-up.md#limits-of-revision-a) lists the figures to measure on the first board.

**Four of the lines**

```text
PASS  5 V cartridge: rail limit: the rail reaches 5.600 V at DAC code 0; the comparator trips at 5.863 V
PASS  trip to switch open: 0.1 ms after the comparator trips; cartridge saw 6.47 V of a 6.5 V fault
PASS  inrush: peak 0.4 A, above 2 A for 0 us; supply side dips to 5.00 V
PASS  discharge (weak AO3400A): cartridge at 0.05 V after the firmware's 50 ms (below 0.5 V after 24.7 ms); supply side left at 4.88 V
```

An earlier circuit failed four of these checks: 24 A of inrush, 17.8 ms to open the switch, no limit between 5.5 V and 5.86 V, and a discharge that depended on the transistor. The switch, its two transistors and the feedback divider were changed until the checks passed.

## Study the supplies and the bus

Five more scripts go beyond nominal values. Each prints `PASS`, `FAIL` and `INFO` lines and exits with status 1 if a check fails. All five fail today: [Open design faults](../guides/bring-up.md#open-design-faults) lists what they found.

| Script | Subject | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hardware/spice/run_tolerance.sh` | The DUT rail and its comparator over part tolerances: 2000 random units and 8192 corners | 3 pass, 6 fail |
| `hardware/spice/run_sequence.sh` | Power-up, a cartridge pulled or plugged under power, brown-out, input-pad leakage | 10 pass, 2 fail |
| `hardware/spice/reg/run.sh` | The regulators as switching converters, and the impedance of the FPGA supplies | 29 pass, 5 fail |
| `hardware/spice/dip/run.sh` | The three supply rails of the DIP cartridge and their order | 11 pass, 7 fail |
| `hardware/spice/si/run.sh` | Overshoot, ringing and delay on the bus lines from the FPGA to the socket and back | 7 pass, 15 fail |

The regulator model is this project's own, built from the datasheets, because the manufacturer publishes no SPICE model. Its loop compensation is assumed, so the stability results are indicative. The bus script downloads Texas Instruments' IBIS models for the two buffer types on the first run. The FPGA pad and the DRAM are generic models. The copper length of every bus line is in `hardware/spice/si/lengths.json`, taken from the routed boards.

## Preview the display

**Draw every screen to a PPM file**

```sh
cd firmware
cargo run -p rt-hal --features host --example lcd_preview -- /tmp/lcd
```

**Output**

```text
1-select
2-testing
3-pass
4-fail
5-details
6-no-device
7-about
```

The files use the same fonts and colours as the display.

## Web interface

**Build the page and try it against the simulated tester**

```sh
python3 web/build.py
python3 web/dev.py 8080
```

**Output**

```text
14 files in web/dist, 140129 bytes gzipped in web_assets.h
http://localhost:8080/
```

`web/build.py` downloads the Jupiter stylesheet, fonts and logo with `gh`. `web/dev.py` answers the same requests as the Wi-Fi module and runs the firmware's console against its software model. Post `good`, `edo`, `empty`, `cell` or `short` to `/api/memory` to change the simulated memory.

## Wi-Fi module firmware

**Build with PlatformIO**

```sh
python3 web/build.py
cd wifi
pio run
```

This firmware has not been compiled yet. The ESP32 toolchain needs about 4 GB of disk.

## RP2350 firmware

**Build the binary**

```sh
rustup target add thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf
gateware/build.sh
cd firmware/rt-fw
cargo build --release
```

**Last line of the output**

```text
Finished `release` profile [optimized + debuginfo] target(s)
```

The binary compiles and links. It has not run on a board.

## Build the enclosure

**Enclosure and fit checks**

```sh
cd enclosure
uv venv
uv pip install -e .
.venv/bin/python enclosure.py --check
```

**Last line of the output**

```text
enclosure checks passed
```

The command writes the STEP and STL files to `enclosure/out/`.

## Documentation

The pages are Markdown in `docs-src`. `jupiter-docs` from [belikh/docs](https://github.com/belikh/docs) generates `docs/*.md` and the site from them. Edit `docs-src` only.

**Check and build the pages**

```sh
git clone https://github.com/belikh/docs .jupiter-docs
(cd .jupiter-docs && npm ci && npm run update:design)
export JUPITER_DESIGN_DIR="$PWD/.jupiter-docs/vendor/design"
node .jupiter-docs/packages/docs/bin/jupiter-docs.mjs check
node .jupiter-docs/packages/docs/bin/jupiter-docs.mjs build
```

**Output of the check**

```text
16 page(s) OK
```

Commit `docs-src` and the regenerated `docs` together. `.jupiter-docs` and `dist` are in `.gitignore`.

## Workflows

| Workflow | Runs on | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs.yaml` | Push to `main` and pull request that touch the pages | `jupiter-docs check`, `build --check` and the site build |
